uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Ans.searchText: BOTANY - PLANT SCIENCE Transport in Plants Unlike animals, plants have no heart, no blood and no circulation. However, plants do need a transport system to move food, water and minerals around. To do this they have two different systems – xylem (pronounced ‘zi-lem’) moves water from the roots to the leaves and phloem (pronounced ‘flow-em’) moves food from the leaves to the rest of the plant. uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Ans.searchText: BOTANY - PLANT SCIENCE Fertilisation Pollination is the transfer of pollen from one plant to another, whereas fertilisation is the fusion of male and female gametes. Pollen contains the male gametes (sperm) and the ovary, at the base of the stigma, contains the female gamete (egg cell). They are not true leaves but will photosynthesise for a short time to supply energy so the true leaves can grow. uploads/science/Scipad/Year 9 Book 1/Ans.searchText: BOTANY - PLANT SCIENCE Seed Dispersal A seed contains a new plant and a store of food. Plants produce large numbers of seeds because only a few grow successfully into mature plants. In the wild, most seeds never even get to germinate (start growing). Seed dispersal involves the spreading of seeds over a distance. They need to be dispersed away from the parent plant, or they will suffer from competition for light and space as well as for nutrients
